title: ValidationResult — the versioned four-dimensional result contract
description: Machine contract for specification/validation-result.md, required by TDR-0033. A result names its TDR-0032 conformance subject and the specification it was assessed against, and reports structural, semantic, relational and lifecycle-transition eligibility independently. The object is closed at every level so that no aggregate verdict, standing claim, repair or inferred value can be added: DAC-0033 constraint 8 forbids a normative aggregate green result, and TDR-0027 reserves standing to the authorised human act.

contract_version.description: Version of THIS contract. Independent of the assessed object's specification version — the two version different things.

type.description: The TDR-0032 conformance subject. Two of the seven are deliberately absent. `collection`: TDR-0032 leaves that class architecturally present with no contract and DAC-0032 constraint 6 forbids advertising conformance for it — a result that cannot be governed cannot be issued. `participant`: execution is a behavioural claim made by passing fixtures, corpus and probes, and TDR-0033 is explicit that behavioural conformance is not a validation dimension (DAC-0033 constraint 7). Every subject admitted here has a serialised representation, which is why structural validity is never not-applicable. Conformance at one level implies nothing at another.

id.description: Identifies the object assessed — TDR-0034, records/value, recover-value-records, an implementation name.

specification.description: First-class and required. A result that does not say what it validated against has not made a verifiable claim — the same gap TDR-0032 identified in detached records.

assessed_state.description: The state the object legitimately occupies. Validity is relative to it: information required only for a later transition does not make the current state invalid (TDR-0033).

requested_transition.description: Present only when a transition is actually requested. Its presence or absence governs the legal transition-eligibility results.

context.description: The declared portable evaluation context relational validity ran against — what the validator could see. No register or graph is required; a graph may compute relational validity faster and is not a normative dependency.

unreachable_refs.description: References the context could not reach. These make relational validity indeterminate, never fail — failing them would make offline and zero-install use impossible, and passing them would conceal real organisational inconsistency.

dimensions.description: All four dimensions, always, exactly once each. A dimension cannot be omitted to avoid reporting it, and the four are not a pass pipeline.

validator.description: Who produced the result. Identity only — it confers nothing.

allOf.description: structural validity permits pass, fail or indeterminate. not-applicable would mean no serialised representation formed part of the typed assessment, which this contract version does not admit.
No requested transition => transition-eligibility must be not-applicable.
A requested transition => transition-eligibility must actually be evaluated.

result.description: `indeterminate` is not a softer fail and is never permission to infer the missing fact. `not-applicable` means the dimension or rule does not apply to this object, state, transition or declared evaluation.

unevaluated_because.description: The dimension whose result prevented checks here from running. Dependency is recorded explicitly rather than implied by ordering.

allOf.description: fail, indeterminate and not-applicable each require at least one reason. An unexplained negative is an assertion, not a finding; an indeterminate's reason is its entire content; and not-applicable is the result most easily used to make an inconvenient dimension disappear.

code.description: A stable code a consumer can branch on without parsing prose.

ref.description: The artefact supporting the reason — a schema pointer, a file, a fixture identifier.

locus.description: Where within it — a line, a JSON pointer, a section.
